Isolated eugenol—framed primarily as a clove constituent (90-98%) rather than ground allspice—showed paraquat-rat cognitive/anxiety gains in one series with uncertain cohort independence (Uchewa 2025, PMID:40617359) but was completely null across 14-day oral mouse behavioral assays (NSF, NOR, TST, social interaction; Dhara 2020, PMID:32027395), leaving the claim open.

One randomized parallel trial (Nieman 2022, n=64, raw almonds 57 g/d vs cereal bar) reported a favorable POMS tension interaction during post-exercise recovery (p=0.033; total mood disturbance null p=0.130), and the ATTIS roasted-almond RCT (Dikariyanto 2020, n=105) improved parasympathetic HF-HRV during mental stress (p=0.031). Three competing whole-almond RCTs showed null clinical/mood anxiety effects: Sartori 2026 in 84 adults with mild-to-moderate anxiety/depression (PHQ-ADS P=0.945), Coates 2020 in 128 older adults (POMS tension p=0.991), and Siegel 2023 in 25 adults (POMS-2 tension-anxiety p=0.325, VAS anxiety p=0.642). Zero controlled evidence suggests worsening; the post-exercise tension reduction retains only a minimal_signal easing lean against worsening.

No controlled human or animal study tests roasted almonds for clinical apathy severity in Parkinson's disease or other populations. Whole-almond mood trials (Coates 2020 POMS vigor p=0.163; Siegel 2023 vigor p=0.135; Sartori 2026 PHQ-ADS/WSAS) omitted validated apathy scales.

All five controlled adult almond trials assessing attention or cognitive vigilance reported null between-group attention effects: Coates 2020 (n=128, exact raw whole almonds x 12 wk, Attention RT p=0.347, Accuracy p=0.264, RVIP p=0.924), Dhillon 2017 (n=86, acute post-lunch and 12-week attention null), Adams 2026 (n=33 prediabetes crossover, CANTAB null), Mustra Rakic 2022 (n=60, between-group CANTAB null), and Mohajeri 2026 (n=60 Alzheimer's, MoCA attention p=0.776). Pediatric ADHD trials either lacked placebo (Motaharifard 2019, vs methylphenidate p=0.13/0.47) or bundled sweet almond with raisins alongside methylphenidate with severe baseline imbalance (Mohammadi Kenari 2025, baseline p=0.003). No transferable direction for raw almonds and Parkinson's attention survives.

No controlled human trial tests raw almonds for examiner-rated Parkinson's bradykinesia. Waterborne acetonic almond skin extract in 6-OHDA zebrafish larvae yielded concentration-dependent mixed immobility (Carneiro 2026), mixed-seed rat catalepsy did not isolate almond (Nandagopal 2020), and pediatric ADHD syrup slow-movement AE counts bundled raisins and methylphenidate (Mohammadi Kenari 2025).

Three controlled or within-subject human whole-almond studies point toward easing rather than worsening constipation: Creedon 2022 (NCT03581812, n=87, exact raw Nonpareil whole almonds 56 g/d) increased stool frequency (+1.5 vs -1.0 BMs/wk, P=0.034 in Table 5) despite null BSFS and transit time; Sartori 2026 (n=84, 56 g/d whole almonds) reduced hard-stool frequency (0.0 vs 0.1 stools/d, P=0.002); and Lambert 2020 (n=20 hemodialysis adults, 40 g/d raw almonds) improved constipation on BSFS and POS-S scores across weeks 2-10. Oral sweet almond oil also reduced elderly Rome IV constipation severity (Faghihi 2022, n=79, p<0.0003). Competing findings include null stool frequency in Burns 2016 (n=58 parents/children), lower fecal moisture in Choo 2021 (n=69, P=0.027), and higher bowel movements plus pain in IBS-D sachets (Darvishmoghadam 2019, n=50). Absence of Parkinson's constipation trials keeps the easing signal at minimal_signal.

No clinical study evaluates roasted almonds on levodopa absorption or daily OFF time in Parkinson's disease. Rat and healthy-human gastric-emptying studies (Gallier 2014, Diella 2018) did not co-administer levodopa or enroll Parkinson's patients.

Two multi-month randomized controlled trials of whole raw almonds reported null effects on validated daytime sleepiness scales: Desai 2026 (n=175 poor sleepers, 60 g/d x 20 wk) found inconclusive Epworth Sleepiness Scale delta change (-2.94 vs -2.54, p=0.592; adjusted endline 6.56 vs 7.65, p=0.096), and Coates 2020 (n=128 older adults, 12 wk) found null Karolinska Sleepiness Score (p=0.892). An acute liquid-preload crossover (Miguens-Gomez 2022) noted lower post-preload sleepiness after insect protein than liquid almond protein without roasted-almond vs neutral control worsening. No interpretable direction survives.

All three randomized controlled trials of whole almonds assessing depressive symptoms were null: Sartori 2026 (n=84 adults with mild-to-moderate anxiety/depression, 56 g/d whole almonds x 12 wk, primary PHQ-ADS P=0.945), Coates 2020 (n=128 older adults, 12 wk, POMS depression p=0.827), and Siegel 2023 (n=25, 8-wk crossover, POMS-2 depression-dejection p=0.456), alongside null POMS total mood disturbance in Nieman 2022 (n=64, p=0.130). Matrix-sibling almond-oil massage, inhalation carrier, and rat forced-swim studies (Round 1 claim 0109) do not supply a transferable oral roasted-almond depression signal, and NCT05323019 terminated at n=6 without results.

Desai 2026 (n=175, 60 g/d raw whole almonds x 20 wk) excluded parasomnias at enrollment and found null adjusted polysomnographic REM latency (158.17 vs 158.20 min, p=0.998) and REM duration (37.30 vs 36.43 min, p=0.776), with no dream-enactment or REM sleep without atonia outcome. No clinical or preclinical study evaluates raw almonds for REM sleep behavior disorder or dream enactment.

Fitri 2025 (n=32 dental students) found acute chewing of 15 g whole almonds raised stimulated salivary flow less than paraffin wax gum (0.60 vs 0.82 mL/min in caries-free; 0.39 vs 0.54 mL/min in caries), measuring post-chewing dental flow rather than spontaneous drooling or Parkinson's sialorrhea. Mohammadi Kenari 2025 recorded pediatric ADHD adverse-event drooling counts of 15/40 with sweet almond-plus-raisin syrup vs 5/40 with placebo (omnibus p=0.008 across three methylphenidate arms, no pairwise test or severity score, bundled with raisins and stimulant therapy). Consistent with Round 1 claims 0188 and 0358, neither study yields a transferable Parkinson's drooling direction for roasted almonds.

No clinical or preclinical study tests roasted almonds for levodopa-induced dyskinesia severity in Parkinson's disease; the Round 1 eltoprazine patent merely listed almond oil as a generic theoretical excipient.

No clinical or animal study evaluates roasted almonds for Parkinson's dystonia severity; prior Round 1 almond-oil leads involved only an unconfirmed topical frankincense diluent case and zebrafish swim behavior.

One 24-week open-label randomized controlled trial in middle-aged adults with prediabetes (Gulati 2026, NCT05322304, n=60) reported improved CANTAB executive function (One Touch Stockings of Cambridge beta=-2.5, 95% CI -4.4 to -0.6, P=0.01) and processing speed with almonds (20% energy) plus diet/exercise vs isocaloric diet/exercise, though concurrent weight and glycemic improvements occurred and raw state was not printed in the abstract. Three competing whole-almond RCTs showed no between-group executive-function benefit: Adams 2026 (n=33 prediabetes crossover, 50 g/d x 5 mo, CANTAB null), Coates 2020 (n=128 older adults, raw whole almonds x 12 wk, Executive Accuracy p=0.693, Peg and Ball p=0.444-0.852), and Mustra Rakic 2022 (n=60 older adults, 6 mo, between-group CANTAB null despite within-arm spatial planning gains at 3 oz/d). No Parkinson's trial exists; Gulati 2026 sustains only a minimal_signal easing lean.

No controlled human or animal study tests raw whole almonds for fall frequency in Parkinson's disease or older adults. Round 1 matrix-sibling leads involved only a non-oral sweet almond oil clothing patch during Thai balance training (Areeudomwong 2023) and 6-OHDA zebrafish larvae (Carneiro 2026).

One randomized parallel trial (Nieman 2022, n=64, 57 g/d raw almonds vs cereal bar) reported consistently lower POMS fatigue across all five post-exercise recovery timepoints (group x time interaction p=0.051; 0h-4d means 7.18 to 1.79 vs 8.55 to 3.68), and an older controlled march trial (Arieli 1985, n=30 untrained) reported delayed subjective exhaustion with almonds versus 50% exhaustion in control and sugar groups (without printed p-values). Competing human trials showed null fatigue effects for whole raw almonds at rest: Coates 2020 (n=128 older adults, POMS fatigue p=0.826, vigor p=0.163) and Siegel 2023 (n=25, POMS-2 fatigue-inertia p=0.198), while d'Unienville 2025 (less taper fatigue P=0.05) bundled almonds with grapes and cranberries. Zero controlled studies show fatigue worsening; Nieman 2022 and Arieli 1985 sustain only a minimal_signal easing lean.

No controlled human trial, observational symptom study, or transferable preclinical assay evaluates raw whole almonds for freezing of gait frequency in Parkinson's disease or non-PD populations; available PD-adjacent almond records (Vieregge 1992 dietary preference survey; Carneiro 2026 zebrafish skin-extract model) do not assess freezing of gait frequency.

No controlled human trial, observational symptom study, or transferable preclinical assay evaluates raw whole almonds for hand dexterity impairment in Parkinson's disease or non-PD populations; available PD-adjacent almond records (Vieregge 1992 dietary preference survey; Carneiro 2026 zebrafish skin-extract model) do not assess hand dexterity impairment.

One 20-week randomized controlled trial in adults with poor sleep (Desai 2026, CTRI/2023/02/049727, n=175 per-protocol analyzed, 60 g/d raw whole almonds vs isocaloric savory snacks) found significantly lower adjusted global PSQI (3.94 vs 4.79, p=0.013), higher PSQI sleep efficiency (94.45% vs 91.85%, p=0.012; unadjusted change +9.7% vs +5.4%, p=0.021), shorter subjective sleep latency (18.46 vs 26.29 min, p=0.016), and higher serum melatonin (p=0.050), though full-cohort polysomnography parameters did not separate (wake during sleep p=0.081, responders p=0.043). An uncontrolled 14-day student study (Ghafarzadeh 2019, n=442, 10 sweet almonds/d) also reported reduced Insomnia Severity Index prevalence (77.6% to 69.2%, Z=-4.679, p<0.001), and Mohajeri 2026 reported improved PSQI in Alzheimer's disease with powdered almond plus rock candy (p<0.001, bundled). Competing evidence includes a 1-year habitual-snacker RCT showing no significant nondietary sleep difference (Brown 2023, n=136, all P>=0.112). Raw-vs-roasted preparation transfer, open-label designs, null full-cohort PSG, and absence of Parkinson's insomnia trials keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

No controlled study tests raw almonds for low voice volume severity in Parkinson's disease; prior Round 1 almond-oil records involved only topical apomorphine carrier patents (WO2010005507A1), topical facial-wrinkle cosmetic trials, or an 1897 intralaryngeal menthol carrier.

No controlled human or animal study isolates roasted almonds for Parkinson's muscle rigidity. Topical sweet almond oil massage had null knee-osteoarthritis stiffness (Doner 2024 p=0.707), and mixed-seed rat catalepsy (Nandagopal 2020) did not isolate almond.
No human or animal study tests dietary raw almonds for olfactory impairment severity in Parkinson's disease; Kadirova 2016 used almond oil strictly as a diagnostic odor-recognition test stimulus.

No human or animal study tests roasted almonds for orthostatic hypotension or orthostatic lightheadedness in Parkinson's disease or other populations. Resting blood pressure responses to almonds are mixed across RCTs: ATTIS (Dikariyanto 2020, n=107, exact whole roasted almonds) and Siegel 2023 (n=25) found no BP change, whereas Coates 2020 (n=128) lowered SBP and Dhillon 2016 (n=86 compliers) lowered DBP (-2.71 mmHg). Resting BP changes do not measure postural BP drops or orthostatic lightheadedness, and BP lowering could theoretically worsen rather than reduce orthostatic symptoms.

Two independent 8-week randomized crossover trials of whole raw almonds (57 g/d vs isocaloric pretzels) after downhill running in middle-aged adults reported lower task-evoked musculoskeletal pain: Rayo 2024 (San Diego, NCT04787718, n=26) found lower VAS pain during maximal contraction (Trial P=0.026; -37% at 24 h P=0.012, -33% at 48 h P=0.038; resting muscle VAS null), and Siegel 2023 (London, n=25) found ~24% lower 72-h cumulative AUC muscle soreness during vertical jump (p<0.05). Competing evidence is substantial: a 4-week parallel eccentric-exercise RCT found null DOMS (Nieman 2022, n=64, p=0.187), and a double-blind IBS-D trial of 40 g/d almond powder sachets vs wheat flour reported worsened abdominal pain (Darvishmoghadam 2019, n=50, p<0.05), attributed to fermentable oligo-fructans in IBS-D. Because two independent whole-almond trials eased somatic musculoskeletal pain whereas worsening occurred only with powdered sachets in FODMAP-sensitive IBS-D, a tentative minimal_signal easing lean survives while opposing visceral-pain risk and absence of roasted-almond or Parkinson's pain trials remain key limits.

Preclinical-only basis, constituent/leaf transfer limits, and absence of ground-seed or Parkinson's trials keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

Two independent controlled human trials of green banana preparations eased constipation or improved bowel regularity: Cassettari 2019 (n=80 children/adolescents with Rome IV functional constipation) showed green banana biomass alone reduced hard stools (BSFS 1-2), straining, painful defecation, and abdominal pain (p<0.05) while cutting laxative doses by 63-87% as an adjunct, though not increasing >3 BM/wk; Chong 2024 (n=60 adults, 14 d) showed green banana powder normalized stool form and bowel regularity (79% vs 65% normal stools day 7). In a 60-day RCT of raw ripe bananas in n=34 healthy women (Mitsou 2011), daily raw banana reduced bloating (p=0.009-0.010) with no adverse effect on evacuation patterns. Competing observational survey data (Muller-Lissner 2005, n=1,088) reflect subjective beliefs that bananas constipate (29-48%) without controlled intake testing, while Sahiwal Pakistan ethnomedicine (Harun 2025, n=125) records raw/powdered banana fruit for constipation. Non-PD cohorts and green-banana vs ripe-raw exposure gaps cap certainty at minimal_signal.

Preclinical pharmacokinetics and bench chemistry establish a plausible levodopa-degradation interaction with raw banana polyphenol oxidase (PPO), but no verified human study measures clinical daily OFF time. In rats (Ogo 2005, n=3/group), co-administering fresh banana juice halved oral levodopa Cmax (17.4 to 8.6 ug/mL) and AUC (1882.8 to 933.5 ug*min/mL, alpha=0.05), whereas a commercial 10% banana drink had no effect; Uesawa 2010 confirmed rapid enzymatic methyldopa degradation by banana pulp in vitro, and Ottaviani 2023 confirmed human in vivo banana-smoothie PPO degradation of flavan-3-ols. Hotozuka 2022 (PMID:35802918) is a paywalled letter without an indexed abstract so clinical OFF-time details remain unverified; Garfinkel 1972 reported black vomit after levodopa with banana without motor OFF tracking; a 2019 Parkinson's UK thread discussed nausea rather than OFF time. All verified quantitative sources have remote outcome fit (PK/chemistry only), keeping the verdict open.

No human clinical trial tests cooked or boiled barley grain for bradykinesia in Parkinson's disease. Five independent human feeding trials consistently indicate that whole cooked/boiled barley and fiber-rich barley preparations ease constipation or increase stool bulk, whereas purified isolated barley beta-glucan extract failed to replicate the effect. Taniguchi 2017 (PMC5319020, n=28 nursing-home elderly, mean age 88.9 y) found boiled Kirarimochi waxy barley increased monthly defecation days (7.1 to 8.9-9.6, p=0.014-0.030) and cut laxative days (6.3 to 4.1, p=0.003-0.018) in the constipated subgroup (n=14) without causing diarrhea in non-constipated residents. Li 2003 (n=10 crossover) increased stool volume, Bird 2008 (n=17 crossover, wholegrain Himalaya 292 barley) increased fecal weight +33% and butyrate +91%, and Kanauchi 1998 (n=16 constipated adults) relieved constipation with germinated barley foodstuff. Inhaled-oil/extract exposure gaps and absence of PD clinical trials cap certainty at minimal_signal.

No controlled human trial, observational cohort, or animal model evaluates ground black pepper for apathy severity in Parkinson's disease or other populations. Three independent preclinical Parkinson's disease rodent models demonstrate that oral piperine — the dominant bioactive alkaloid (5-9% by weight) of black pepper — eases bradykinesia: Liu 2016 (PMC5308619, rotenone PD mice, n=10/group) showed 4 weeks of oral piperine (25-50 mg/kg/d) significantly shortened pole-test descent time (explicitly defined as the bradykinesia assay, p<0.05/p<0.01, comparable to L-dopa) and improved rotarod latency via PP2A-mediated autophagy; Li 2022 (PMID:34092198, PMC9037522, Thy1-SNCA alpha-synuclein transgenic PD mice) showed oral piperine (25-100 mg/kg/d) shortened pole-test bradykinesia time and preserved rotarod performance via P2RX4 autophagy flux; Hu 2024 (PMC10848080, 6-OHDA PD rats, n=5-6/group) showed oral piperine (20 mg/kg/d x 6 wk) alone attenuated 6-OHDA lesions and with L-dopa markedly improved open-field bradykinesia velocity and distance by inhibiting gut Enterococcus faecalis tyrosine decarboxylase. Corroborated by motor-coordination gains in Shrivastava 2013 (6-OHDA rats) and Yang 2015 (MPTP mice). Competing minor-constituent nuance: trace black pepper N-isobutylamide guineensine (2.5-5 mg/kg i.p.) acutely induced catalepsy and hypolocomotion in healthy mice (Nicolussi 2014, Reynoso-Moreno 2017; abolished in LPS endotoxemia). Isolated-constituent animal models with zero human PD trials cap certainty at minimal_signal toward easing (contradicting the "worsens" hypothesis).

No controlled trial establishes whether ground black pepper worsens or eases excessive daytime sleepiness in Parkinson's disease. Varoni 2026 (PMC13207175, uncontrolled case series, n=14 completers of burning mouth syndrome) reported Epworth Sleepiness Scale scores falling from a normal baseline of 3.86+/-3.16 to 2.86+/-2.96 (Wilcoxon p=0.015) after an expectorated 10 mg topical piperine mouthrinse, which is uncontrolled, non-ingested, below the clinical sleepiness threshold (>10), and confounded by oral pain relief. Conversely, direct oral 2.0 g black pepper capsules were null on alertness/energy/fatigue in Lindheimer 2013 (n=40 RCT), and bundled curcumin + piperine was null on daytime sleepiness in Seyedabadi 2023 (n=117 RCT).

Six independent controlled rodent studies across four behavioral despair/stress paradigms consistently show antidepressant-like effects from Piper nigrum fruit extract and isolated piperine: Guan 2025 (PMC11899911, sleep-deprived mice, ethanolic Piper nigrum extract 75-300 mg/kg reduced FST/TST immobility), Wattanathorn 2008 (Wistar rats, oral piperine 5-20 mg/kg x 4 wk), Mao 2014 (PMC11488929, CUMS rats, reversed sucrose-preference loss and FST immobility with 5-HT/BDNF restoration), Li 2007 (PMID:17289085 & PMID:17701559, CMS/FST/TST mice, active at 2.5-20 mg/kg without locomotor confounding but null at 80 mg/kg), Hu 2009 (n=60 CUMS rats, 10-20 mg/kg restored sucrose preference and lowered ACTH/CRH), and Basavaraju 2023 (LPS mice, nanopiperine 5-10 mg/kg). Preclinical extract/piperine models without isolated human clinical trials cap certainty at minimal_signal.

Rodent Morris water maze studies (Guan 2025, Yang 2015, Wang 2019, Wattanathorn 2008) test spatial memory in animals and do not override null human oral black pepper cognitive trials.

Preclinical PD models of oral piperine (Shrivastava 2013 narrow beam/rotarod; Liu 2016 rotarod) also trend toward better motor balance. Inhaled essential oil (not oral cracked pepper), acute laboratory sway metrics, GRADE very-low certainty, and absence of Parkinson's postural-instability trials cap certainty at minimal_signal.

Two non-PD controlled trials support a modest easing signal: Steptoe 2007 (n=75 men, 6-wk DB RCT of 4 cups/d brewed black tea vs caffeinated placebo) significantly increased post-stress subjective relaxation (p=0.036) and lowered post-stress cortisol (p=0.032), while Staack 2022 (n=56 completed OAB women, DB crossover) found 400 mg/d caffeine reduced Beck Anxiety Inventory scores (p<0.05; bridged via Ayakdaş 2025 chromatography). However, PD caffeine RCTs (Postuma 2012 n=61; Postuma 2017 n=118) and Sauerbier 2018 (n=139 PD HADS) showed null anxiety contrasts, and acute task stress in Steptoe 2007 was unchanged; evidence is capped at minimal_signal.

No clinical trial or controlled observational study has directly evaluated brewed black tea on apathy severity in Parkinson disease. Café-PD (Postuma 2017, n=118) reported no standalone apathy improvement, Sauerbier 2018 (n=139) found no tea association with NMSS mood/apathy, and 1596 herbal descriptions (Li Shizhen) provide only non-clinical cultural context. Because direct brewed-tea human evidence for apathy severity is absent, the claim remains open.

Multiple double-blind crossover trials of brewed black tea in healthy adults demonstrate acute improvements in objective attention and vigilance: De Bruin 2011 (two crossovers, n=26 and n=32) improved switch-task accuracy (p<0.002 and p=0.007) and auditory (p<0.001) and visual (p=0.030) intersensory attention, and Hindmarch 1998 (n=19) and Hindmarch 2000 (n=30) sustained critical flicker fusion and psychomotor vigilance across the day. Tempered by null single-cup black tea RVRT in Kahathuduwa 2017 (n=20, p=0.429), slight global MoCA worsening with chronic caffeine capsules in PD (Postuma 2017, -0.66 pts, not separated to attention), and absence of PD brewed-tea attention RCTs; rated minimal_signal (eases -> Maybe False against the worsening statement).

Bingham 1997 (n=65 healthy adults, 4-wk randomized crossover of 6 mugs/day brewed black tea vs caffeine-matched placebo, adherence verified by urinary PABA) found brewed black tea significantly softened stool consistency (p=0.04), opposing the claim that brewed black tea worsens constipation. Counterbalancing context includes Doustfatemeh 2017 (n=120 pediatric acute nonbacterial diarrhea RCT where black tea tablets firmed diarrheal stools, p<0.001—a distinct acute diarrheal condition and tablet prep), null PD NMSS GI associations in Sauerbier 2018 (n=139), and a recruiting L-theanine PD GI trial without results (NCT07682532). Rated minimal_signal (eases -> Maybe False).

No clinical trial or controlled observational study has directly evaluated brewed black tea on daily off time in Parkinson disease. Postuma 2012 (n=61, 34 with fluctuations) and Café-PD (Postuma 2017, n=118) found no significant improvement in motor fluctuations with caffeine capsules, and Deleu 2006 (n=12) tested only acute single-dose levodopa onset latency rather than daily off-time hours. Because direct brewed-tea human evidence for daily off time is absent, the claim remains open.

Two multicenter double-blind placebo-controlled Parkinson disease trials of isolated caffeine capsules—bridged to brewed black tea via Ayakdaş 2025 infusion chromatography (24-39 mg caffeine/200 mL)—demonstrate modest, attenuating reductions in PD daytime sleepiness: Postuma 2012 (n=61 somnolent PD) improved CGI-C somnolence (+0.64, 95% CI 0.16 to 1.13) and per-protocol ESS (-1.97, -3.87 to -0.05; ITT ESS -1.71, -3.57 to 0.13), and Café-PD (Postuma 2017, n=118 analyzed PD) improved 6-month MDS-UPDRS 1.8 daytime sleepiness (-0.49, -0.79 to -0.20) and 3-month SCOPA-sleep daytime (-1.09, -1.88 to -0.30) before attenuating at 12-18 months. Direct brewed black tea crossovers in non-PD adults (De Bruin 2011 n=58; Hindmarch 1998 n=19; Hindmarch 2000 n=30) corroborate acute alertness and anti-sedation benefits. Because PD RCTs tested capsules rather than brewed black tea, evidence qualifies for limited_clinical_link (eases -> Maybe False against the worsening statement).

Two non-PD sources provide a weak easing signal: the Guangzhou Biobank Cohort Study (Chen 2022, n=10,014 older adults) found regular tea drinkers had lower GDS-15 depressive symptom scores (beta -0.60, 95% CI -0.78 to -0.42; OR 0.51, 0.35-0.72) consistently across black, green, and oolong tea, and Shamabadi 2023 (n=50 completed MDD adults, 6-wk DB RCT) showed L-theanine 200 mg/d + sertraline outperformed placebo + sertraline on HDRS (time-by-treatment p=0.014; wk 6 p=0.01; bridged via Ayakdaş 2025 chromatography, noting much lower L-theanine per tea cup). Tempered by null BDI outcomes in PD caffeine RCTs (Postuma 2012 n=61; Postuma 2017 n=118—both excluding moderate-to-severe baseline depression), Staack 2022 (n=56 BDI null), and Sauerbier 2018 (n=139 PD HADS null); rated minimal_signal.

No clinical trial or controlled observational study has directly evaluated brewed black tea on drooling severity in Parkinson disease. In the multicenter double-blind Café-PD trial (Postuma 2017, n=118 analyzed PD, caffeine 200 mg BID vs placebo, bridged to brewed black tea by Ayakdaş 2025 chromatography), caffeine modestly worsened MDS-UPDRS 4.1+4.2 dyskinesia scores across combined time points (+0.25 pts, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.45; +0.28 [0.01 to 0.55] at 3 mo, +0.12 [-0.17 to 0.41] at 6 mo, +0.36 [0.02 to 0.70] at 18 mo). Historical clinical challenge data (Shoulson & Chase 1975, n=6 PD) similarly reported longer levodopa-related dyskinesia duration with concurrent caffeine. Competing evidence includes null 6-week dyskinesia in Postuma 2012 (n=61, only 14/61 with baseline dyskinesia) and observational baseline coffee analysis in CALM-PD (Wills 2013: HR 0.61 [0.37-1.01] for >12 oz/d, HR 0.73 [0.46-1.15] for 4-12 oz/d, CIs crossing 1.0). Because Café-PD directly assessed dyskinesia in diagnosed human PD using isolated caffeine capsules rather than brewed tea, evidence qualifies for limited_clinical_link (worsens -> Maybe False against the reduces statement).

Because direct brewed-tea human evidence for dystonia severity is absent, the claim remains open.

Two double-blind randomized crossover trials of brewed black tea in healthy adults (De Bruin 2011, study 1 n=26 and study 2 n=32) significantly enhanced executive attention-switching task accuracy vs matched hot-water placebo (p<0.002 and p=0.007), corroborated by the Payne 2025 meta-analysis of L-theanine + caffeine interventions (AST accuracy h1 SMD 0.40 p=0.004; h2 SMD 0.33 p=0.008). Tempered by Café-PD (Postuma 2017, n=118 PD) where chronic caffeine capsules yielded slightly worse global MoCA scores (-0.66 pts, 95% CI -1.32 to -0.01; global screen not isolated to executive function) and absence of PD brewed-tea executive trials; rated minimal_signal.

Because direct brewed-tea human evidence for fall frequency is absent, the claim remains open.

In Postuma 2012 (n=61 PD, bridged to brewed black tea via Ayakdaş 2025 chromatography), caffeine capsules yielded Fatigue Severity Scale point estimates in the easing direction (-3.08 pts [95% CrI -6.88 to +0.73] at wk 3; -2.85 [-7.73 to +2.06] at wk 6) with credible intervals spanning zero (reliability_fit="remote", matching Round 1 coffee fatigue precedent 0121). Direct brewed black tea crossovers in healthy adults (De Bruin 2011 n=58; Hindmarch 1998 n=19; Hindmarch 2000 n=30) reduced subjective sedation and raised alertness. Tempered by null PD observational fatigue findings in Alshimemeri 2026 (n=131 PD FSS survey), Sauerbier 2018 (n=139 NMSS sleep/fatigue), and the MVP 2024 baseline heatmap (black tea at zero swatch); rated minimal_signal (eases -> Maybe False).

Kitagawa 2007 evaluated oral caffeine 100 mg/day (bridged to ~2.5-4 cups brewed black tea via Ayakdaş 2025 chromatography) in people with Parkinson disease and freezing of gait (FOG), reporting improvement in the "total akinesia" FOG subtype (no benefit in "trembling in place"), with tolerance developing within months and restoration after a 2-week withdrawal. Because Kitagawa 2007 was uncontrolled with exact sample size and quantitative FOG scores unavailable in the indexed abstract (reliability_fit="remote"), and Postuma 2012/2017 showed null general UPDRS gait/motor outcomes without isolating FOG frequency, evidence is capped at minimal_signal.

Daytime-only dosing trials found no sleep penalty (Postuma 2012 PSQI -0.29 [-1.42 to 0.84]; Staack 2022 ISI null; Zhang 2020 daytime oolong/caffeine PSG null). Rated minimal_signal (worsens -> Maybe False against the reduces statement).

Two independent non-PD randomized trials favor anxiety reduction: Venable 2025 (NCT04398784; n=45 enrolled / 21 paired GAD-7 completers with MDD/GAD; 12-wk DB crossover of 24 g/d whole freeze-dried blueberry powder) lowered GAD-7 vs placebo (-3.134 +/- 1.476, p=0.035 ITT; -3.67 pts, p=0.02, d=0.54 completers; 6-wk null p=0.0987), and Sinclair 2022 (n=45 randomized / 44 completed healthy adults; 20-d juice concentrate) lowered STAI state (b=5.76, p=0.018) and trait anxiety (b=7.18, p=0.023), alongside postprandial calmness improvement in Curtis 2024 (+11.6%, p=0.01, q=0.04; 6-mo null). Crucially, opposing trial Velichkov 2024 (NCT04647019; n=60 depressed emerging adults, 6-wk wild blueberry powder) showed worse GAD-7 vs placebo (7.5 vs 5.4, p=0.026), and Fisk 2020 (n=64 adolescents) was null on RCADS anxiety. Because two RCTs (including clinically diagnosed GAD/MDD) favor easing against one opposing emerging-adult trial and zero PD trials, evidence yields a fragile minimal_signal (eases -> Maybe False against the worsening statement).

Because direct or transferable human efficacy evidence for apathy severity is absent, the claim stays open.

No human clinical trial has tested raw or roasted Brazil nuts on anxiety severity, and the largest older-adult selenium RCT (Rayman 2006, PMID16181615, n=501 aged 60-74 y, 6 mo of 100-300 ug/d Se) found completely null POMS-BI mood/anxiety results (F=0.25, p=0.86). Three independent rodent studies support an anxiolytic signal: Kaur 2021 demonstrated anxiolytic activity of Brassica oleracea broccoli floret extract and its isolated kaempferol-3-O-beta-D-glucoside (0.061% w/w) across EPM, hole-board, and mirror chamber tests, while Wu 2016 (CMS mice, OFT/NSF) and Ferreira-Chamorro 2018 (CCI neuropathic pain mice) showed anxiolytic effects of sulforaphane (bridged to raw broccoli via Conaway 2000 32.3% ITC bioavailability). Human evidence is indirect and mixed: Nouchi 2022 (n=144) lowered overall POMS2 negative mood without isolating anxiety, Wang 2025 ASD meta-analysis reported null anxiety, and no PD anxiety trial exists; capped at minimal_signal.

No clinical trial tests roasted broccoli on Parkinson apathy severity, and human sulforaphane schizophrenia trials conflict on negative symptoms: NCT04521868 (Huang 2025 n=77; companion Chen 2025 n=42) reported PANSS negative-symptom reduction (p=0.01, 24-wk d=0.8), whereas the larger first-episode trial Hei 2022 (n=172) found null PANSS scores, Kassar 2025 meta-analysis (4 RCTs, n=369) found 12-wk negative-symptom gain (p=0.02) was not sustained at endpoint, and Okazaki 2026 meta-analysis found no pooled efficacy difference. Wright 2024 PD self-experiments (8/10 apathy/mood attenuation) bundled broccoli seed tea with mustard without control, and roasting denatures myrosinase (~3x lower sulforaphane yield, Conaway 2000). Direction remains open.

Three independent rodent Parkinson toxin models support a minimal preclinical easing signal for purified sulforaphane: Zhou 2016 (rotenone PD mice) rescued spontaneous cylinder hind-limb stepping and challenging beam traversal alongside striatal TH preservation, Morroni 2013 (6-OHDA PD mice) ameliorated motor coordination deficits and rotations, and Xie 2026 (MPTP PD mice) improved motor performance and nigral TH+ neuron survival, bridged to raw broccoli by Conaway 2000 (32.3% ITC bioavailability with intact myrosinase). However, Wright 2024 reported 0/13 symptomatic bradykinesia responses in PD volunteers drinking weekly broccoli seed tea plus mustard over 4-6 weeks, and PD RCT NCT05084365 has no posted results; capped at minimal_signal.

Controlled human and animal studies support an easing direction: Yanaka 2018 (UMIN000021207, n=48 constipated adults with CSS>2) found 20 g/d raw broccoli sprouts for 4 weeks significantly reduced total CSS (7.25 to 5.17, p=0.0017; sustained at 4-wk washout) and defecation attempt duration (p=0.0077) whereas alfalfa sprouts did not, and Duan 2023 showed oral broccoli-derived exosome-like nanoparticles relieved loperamide-induced constipation in mice. Contextual PD logs (Wright 2024: 9/11 constipation attenuation on BST+mustard) and multi-ingredient broccoli fiber trials (Woo 2015 n=96; Hughes 2002 n=11) align directionally, but mature raw broccoli florets have not been isolated in a PD constipation RCT; capped at minimal_signal.

Forsberg 2022 surveyed vegetable finger-food preferences among Swedish older adults with motoric eating difficulties including PD (broccoli was well liked) without measuring dexterity change. Uncontrolled PD broccoli-seed-plus-mustard tea logs (Wright 2024) reported 0/13 rigidity responses over 4-6 weeks, while rodent PD models (Zhou 2016, Morroni 2013, Xie 2026) evaluated cylinder stepping, beam traversal, rotations, and general motor coordination without direct rigidity or catalepsy scoring, and PD trial NCT05084365 has no posted results. Direction remains open.

No human clinical trial or Parkinson animal olfaction study evaluates steamed broccoli or sulforaphane on olfactory impairment severity; Wright 2024 Table 1 single case had baseline smell score 0 unchanged, and steaming lowers sulforaphane yield ~3-fold (Conaway 2000).

No human clinical trial or autonomic study evaluates steamed broccoli or sulforaphane on orthostatic hypotension or orthostatic lightheadedness in Parkinson disease; Mirmiran 2014 (PMID:24940565) lowered seated BP only when broccoli sprout powder was combined with H. pylori triple therapy.

A randomized human broccoli dietary trial and three independent mouse pain models converge on an easing (antinociceptive) signal opposing the worsening hypothesis: the BRIO double-blind feasibility RCT (Davidson 2024, NCT03878368, n=24 knee OA) found 12 weeks of high-glucoraphanin broccoli soup reduced WOMAC pain by 4.2 points (95% CI 1.03-7.38) vs matched placebo soup (bridged by Davidson 2017 n=40 demonstrating synovial-fluid ITC delivery and Conaway 2000 showing ~3x higher ITC bioavailability from raw vs cooked broccoli). Preclinical models confirm sulforaphane reverses neuropathic (Ferreira-Chamorro 2018 CCI p<0.001; McDonnell 2017 diabetic db/db) and inflammatory (Redondo 2017 CFA) allodynia and hyperalgesia. Limits: small OA feasibility preprint, cooked soup vs raw florets, and non-PD pain cap certainty at minimal_signal.

Two independent rodent Parkinson models support a minimal preclinical easing signal for sulforaphane on postural balance and motor coordination: Zhou 2016 showed sulforaphane rescued challenging narrow-beam traversal (postural balance/sensorimotor integration) in rotenone PD mice (n=3/group in behavior panels), and Morroni 2013 showed sulforaphane ameliorated motor coordination deficits in 6-OHDA PD mice. Conaway 2000 confirms heat-cooked broccoli retains ~10.2% sulforaphane bioavailability via gut microbial hydrolysis (though ~3x lower than raw due to myrosinase denaturation). Tempered by Wright 2024's lack of overall motor attenuation in PD BST+mustard self-experiments and absence of human PD postural RCTs; capped at minimal_signal.
No human clinical trial or observational study evaluates roasted broccoli or sulforaphane on hypomimia/reduced facial expressiveness in Parkinson disease; NCT05084365 lacks posted results.

No controlled clinical or animal study isolates an effect of roasted broccoli or sulforaphane on Parkinson rest tremor. In Wright 2024's uncontrolled PD broccoli-seed-plus-mustard tea logs, only 1/10 tremor cases reported attenuation while prose noted slight transient tremor increases in a few participants, and Ayurvedic commentary (Mulye 2024) discusses excess pungent brassicas/mustard as a class without testing broccoli. Roasting also denatures myrosinase (Conaway 2000), and NCT05084365 has no posted results. Direction remains open.

No clinical trial or rodent Parkinson stride-length study tests roasted broccoli or sulforaphane on shortened stride severity; Javaheri 2017 assessed osteoarthritis gait asymmetry (not PD stride length) with synthetic SFX-01, and Wright 2024 found no motor attenuation.

No human trial evaluates roasted broccoli or sulforaphane on Parkinson micrographia/small handwriting severity; Wright 2024 Table 1 single-case ID 415 recorded handwriting unchanged at 1/3 across all 6 weeks on uncontrolled BST+mustard.

No human clinical study evaluates roasted broccoli or sulforaphane on Parkinson dysarthria or speech intelligibility impairment; Wright 2024 Table 1 single case had baseline speech score 0 unchanged, and NCT05084365 lacks posted results.

No clinical study tests raw broccoli consumption on Parkinson swallowing difficulty (dysphagia) severity. Baert 2021 (n=36-47 PD + controls) used broccoli soup solely as a carrier to compare sensory intensity and texture preference across gum vs starch liquid thickeners without assessing raw broccoli or clinical swallowing safety/dysphagia severity. Direction remains open.

No controlled clinical or preclinical trial tests roasted broccoli or sulforaphane on urinary urgency frequency. Wright 2024's patient-led PD logs reported high attenuation of urinary urgency in 13/14 cases drinking weekly boiled broccoli seed tea plus 10-15% white mustard seed powder (while also noting temporary worsening of urinary urgency when exceeding the weekly dose), but the uncontrolled, unblinded, co-exposed design has remote attribution and exposure and cannot sign the claim under v1 rubric rules. van Die 2017 (n=22) tested a 4-herb prostate blend with null IPSS, and roasting denatures myrosinase (Conaway 2000). Direction remains open.

No clinical or preclinical study evaluates steamed broccoli or sulforaphane on Parkinson visual hallucination frequency; schizophrenia sulforaphane meta-analyses (Kassar 2025, Okazaki 2026) found no effect on PANSS positive psychotic symptoms, and steaming lowers sulforaphane bioavailability ~3-fold (Conaway 2000).

No human trial tests roasted broccoli on walking slowness in Parkinson disease. Preclinical studies are indirect: Zhou 2016 rescued challenging narrow-beam traversal time in rotenone PD mice with injected sulforaphane (n=3/group), and Javaheri 2017 prevented osteoarthritis gait asymmetry (not speed) with synthetic SFX-01 in STR/Ort mice. Meanwhile, Wright 2024 reported no general motor benefit (1/36 motor responses) in PD broccoli-seed-tea logs, roasting reduces sulforaphane yield ~3-fold (Conaway 2000), and PD trials NCT05084365 and NCT07360977 lack posted results. Direction remains open.

One human double-blind RCT and one mouse stress model support an easing signal for brown-rice-derived preparations: Lee 2026 (n=80 stressed adults) showed 8 weeks of GABA-enriched fermented rice germ extract significantly lowered Stress Response Inventory scores vs placebo (-5.39 points, 95% CI -10.25 to -0.54, p=0.035), and Tyagi 2025 showed L. reuteri-fermented brown rice reduced corticosterone and anxiety-like behavior in chronic mild stress mice. Tempered by Huh 2025 (n=97 completed rice bran extract RCT) finding only a non-significant trend on K-BAI anxiety and by major processing/population gaps (fermented extracts vs steamed whole brown rice; non-PD adults); capped at minimal_signal.

Two randomized controlled trials of cooked ultra-high hydrostatic pressurized whole brown rice (UHHPBR/UBR) vs polished white rice in older Japanese adults directly support an apathy-easing signal: Matsuzaki 2025 (UMIN000053587, n=44, 12 months) significantly lowered Starkstein Apathy Scale scores vs white rice (p=0.008), replicating Kuroda 2019 (n=52, 24 months, 100 g/d UHHPBR) which also reported reduced Apathy Scale scores alongside faster CADi processing speed. Both trials come from the same Shimane University research group, used pressurized cooked brown rice rather than ordinary home-cooked grain, and enrolled healthy older adults rather than Parkinson patients; capped at minimal_signal.

Direct human attention evidence for brown rice is null or unfavorable against pigmented rice: Gruneck 2022 (n=127 Thai school-aged children) found Sinlek brown rice produced NO improvement on the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT, sustained attention) or Corsi working memory, and Mekhora 2026 (n=24 older adults crossover) found brown rice control underperformed anthocyanin-rich black rice on digit span backward (p=0.03) and verbal recall. Although Kuroda 2019 (n=52) and Matsuzaki 2025 (n=44) reported faster CADi execution time with pressurized brown rice vs white rice, neither isolated a dedicated clinical attention-impairment scale. Direction remains open.

Consistent with Round 1 postural instability (0471=open), no human Parkinson study tests cooked brown rice on bradykinesia severity, and preclinical models remain insufficient to carry a direction: Chompoopong 2016's rotenone PD rat study found germinated brown rice increased open-field ambulation but did NOT achieve statistical significance on mobility duration or pole-test turn/descent times (the classic rodent bradykinesia assay); Uthman 2025 and overlapping Yankuzo 2025 used an invertebrate iron-fed Drosophila climbing assay; and Nagarajan 2015 tested isolated ferulic acid (ubiquitous across wheat and oats) in MPTP mice. Direction remains open.

Converging controlled human clinical trials directly oppose the worsening hypothesis and support an easing signal for cooked brown rice and its bran fraction: Jung 2020 (NCT01933100, n=39 randomized/35 analyzed young women with functional constipation) showed 4 weeks of a cooked brown rice-based diet significantly shortened total colonic transit time vs white rice (-16.5 +/- 8.1 vs +6.8 +/- 2.1 h, between-group p=0.028) and increased within-group stool frequency (3.4 to 5.0/wk, p=0.002); Ghorbani 2025 (n=50 MetS RCT) found 15 g/d brown rice bran powder significantly reduced GSRS constipation rate (p=0.018, ES -0.85); and Adachi 2026 (n=29 CKD single-arm) improved CSS scores (p=0.023) with fermented brown rice. Tempered by Tang 2026 (n=99 fermented brown rice milk DB RCT) showing null primary CSBM/BMF despite significant relief of straining, bloating, and abdominal pain (all p<0.05), and absence of a diagnosed PD constipation RCT; capped at minimal_signal.

No clinical or pharmacokinetic study tests steamed brown rice on levodopa absorption or daily off time in Parkinson disease; Brain Bites PD (ACTRN12625000607471p) lists brown rice only as an optional meal-box example without results.

Two human clinical trials support an easing signal for brown-rice preparations on daytime sleepiness: Um 2019 (KCT0001893, n=42 analyzed DB placebo-controlled RCT in sleep-disturbed adults) found 1,000 mg/d rice bran extract for 2 weeks significantly reduced Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) scores vs placebo (-2.3 +/- 3.9 vs +0.3 +/- 3.5; unadjusted p=0.027, caffeine-adjusted p=0.045), though baseline ESS was higher in the active arm (10.1 vs 6.7, p=0.007). Independently, UMIN000056929 (2025 open randomized crossover in n=15 young women) qualitatively reported lower post-lunch Stanford Sleepiness Scale drowsiness after retort-packaged brown rice vs white rice without posting arm means or p-values. Non-PD samples, extract/retort preparation gaps, and reporting/baseline limits cap certainty at minimal_signal.

Three independent human RCTs and a mouse depression study support an easing signal for brown rice and rice bran: Huh 2025 (NCT05180136, n=97 completed DB placebo-controlled RCT in mild-to-moderate depressed adults) showed 1 g/d rice bran extract for 8 weeks significantly lowered K-HDRS (-5.73 ITT / -5.95 PP, p<0.001) and K-PHQ-9 (p=0.026 PP); Sakamoto 2007 (n=41 lactating mothers RCT) found 2 weeks of cooked pre-germinated brown rice vs white rice decreased POMS depression and total mood disturbance; Mahdavi-Roshan 2025 (n=43 open-label MetS RCT secondary analysis) found 15 g/d brown rice bran powder lowered Beck Depression Inventory (p<=0.05, ES -0.98); and Mamiya 2007 showed pre-germinated brown rice lowered mouse FST/learned-helplessness depression. Tempered by null Zung SDS depression effects in healthy older-adult UHHPBR trials (Kuroda 2019, Matsuzaki 2025) and lack of a PD depression RCT; capped at minimal_signal.

No human or animal study tests steamed brown rice on drooling/sialorrhea severity in Parkinson disease; Apperley 2017 tested a rice-bran saliva-substitute spray for dry mouth (opposite of sialorrhea).
No clinical trial or mammalian levodopa-induced dyskinesia model tests steamed brown rice on dyskinesia severity in Parkinson disease.
No human clinical trial or Parkinson dystonia model tests steamed brown rice on dystonia severity; haloperidol rat catalepsy/vacuous-chewing studies used red rice bran oil rather than steamed grain.

Two randomized controlled trials of cooked ultra-high hydrostatic pressurized brown rice (UHHPBR/UBR) vs polished white rice in older Japanese adults provide a minimal easing signal on frontal/processing-speed cognition: Kuroda 2019 (n=52, 24 months, 100 g/d) improved Frontal Assessment Battery (FAB) sub-item 1 change and shortened CADi processing time, and Matsuzaki 2025 (n=44, 12 months) improved CADi total score/execution time (p<0.05) and adjusted MMSE (p=0.046). However, Lopresti 2025 (n=91 DB RCT of rice bran tocotrienols) found null self-reported executive function despite memory gains, Mekhora 2026 (n=24) showed black rice outperformed brown rice on digit span backward with null Stroop, Uenobe 2019 (n=31 dewaxed brown rice) was null overall on HDS-R (p=0.844; low-cognition subgroup p=0.001), and no PD executive trial exists; capped at minimal_signal.

No human clinical trial tests steamed brown rice on fall frequency in Parkinson disease; Matsuzaki 2025 showed higher calcaneal quantitative ultrasound %YAM bone status with pressurized brown rice in healthy older adults without tracking falls.

Three independent human RCTs support a fatigue-easing signal for cooked pre-germinated brown rice and rice bran arabinoxylan: Sakamoto 2007 (n=41 lactating mothers) showed 2 weeks of cooked pre-germinated brown rice vs white rice significantly decreased POMS fatigue; Ooi 2026 (ACTRN12619000562178p, n=29 DB RCT in cancer patients on systemic therapy) found 3 g/d rice bran arabinoxylan compound for 24 weeks resulted in significantly better fatigue scores than placebo (p<0.05); and Elsaid 2020 (n=60 DB RCT in older adults >56 y) showed 250 mg/d Biobran rice bran arabinoxylan significantly enhanced SF-12v2 vitality. Tempered by Um 2019 (n=42 analyzed 2-week rice bran extract sleep RCT) finding no between-group Fatigue Severity Scale difference and by processing/non-PD population gaps; capped at minimal_signal.
No clinical or preclinical study tests steamed brown rice on freezing of gait frequency in Parkinson disease.
No clinical or preclinical study tests steamed brown rice on hand dexterity impairment in Parkinson disease.

Three independent double-blind, placebo-controlled human RCTs of brown-rice bran and unpolished rice-germ extracts oppose the worsening hypothesis and support sleep improvement: Um 2019 (KCT0001893, n=42 analyzed sleep-disturbed adults) showed 1,000 mg/d rice bran extract improved PSG sleep latency (adjusted p=0.047), total sleep time (+11.7 vs -7.8 min, p=0.019), and sleep efficiency (adjusted p=0.010; PSQI null p=0.510); Byun 2018 (n=40 insomnia symptoms) showed 300 mg/d fermented unpolished rice-germ GABA shortened PSG sleep latency (13.4 to 5.7 min, interaction p=0.009); and Lopresti 2025 (n=91) showed 100 mg/d rice bran tocotrienols reduced sleep disturbance (p=0.015). Tempered by Wagner 2023 (n=188 lifestyle intervention raising brown rice without changing actigraphy sleep), Yoon 2022 (low-dose 75 mg/d rice-germ GABA null REM/PLM), extract vs cooked whole-grain preparation gaps, and non-PD cohorts; capped at minimal_signal.
No clinical or preclinical study evaluates cooked brown rice on hypophonia/low voice volume severity in Parkinson disease.

No human trial tests steamed brown rice on Parkinson muscle rigidity severity. A haloperidol rat study of unrefined red rice bran oil (Naz & Shireen 2014, reviewed in PMID:27540314) reported lower haloperidol catalepsy during weeks 2-5 alongside an internally inconsistent increase in catalepsy in water-only controls, unclear per-arm counts, and an oil matrix remote from steamed whole grain; Chompoopong 2016 did not separately quantify rigidity in rotenone rats. Direction remains open.
No human trial or Parkinson olfaction model evaluates steamed brown rice on olfactory impairment severity.

Three independent double-blind human RCTs of brown-rice-derived bran and fermented preparations oppose the worsening hypothesis and support a pain-easing direction: Elsaid 2020 (n=60 healthy older adults >56 y) showed 3 months of 250 mg/d Biobran rice bran arabinoxylan significantly improved SF-12v2 bodily pain vs placebo; Ooi 2026 (n=29 cancer patients on systemic therapy) found 24 weeks of 3 g/d rice bran arabinoxylan resulted in significantly better pain scores than placebo (p<0.05); and Tang 2026 (n=99 functional constipation) showed fermented brown rice milk significantly relieved abdominal pain vs control (p<0.05). Because all trials tested processed bran extracts or fermented beverages rather than steamed whole grain and none enrolled Parkinson patients, certainty is capped at minimal_signal.
No clinical or observational study evaluates cooked brown rice on hypomimia/reduced facial expressiveness in Parkinson disease.
No clinical trial or Parkinson tremor model tests cooked brown rice on rest tremor severity; Chompoopong 2016 rotenone rats and Uthman 2025 Drosophila did not measure rest tremor.

No clinical trial evaluates cooked brown rice on Parkinson dysphagia or swallowing difficulty severity. Apperley 2017 (n=40 adults with post-radiation xerostomia) tested a multi-ingredient rice-bran emulsion spray and found no clear difference on the Test of Masticating and Swallowing Solids (TOMASS) vs cellulose or water, while Uenobe 2019 (PMC6848844) noted in background commentary that ordinary cooked brown rice is hard to chew and poorly suited to older adults with impaired chewing or swallowing unless dewaxed or cooked as soft porridge. Direction remains open.

Three direct human randomized controlled trials of Agaricus bisporus (total n=471 analyzed) found completely null effects on anxiety: Zajac 2020 (n=370 ITT, 24-wk white button mushroom capsules) was null on DASS-21 anxiety, Glover 2025 (n=41, 6-wk 168 g/d fresh cremini A. bisporus) was null on GAD-7 and POMS tension, and Uffelman 2024 (n=60, 8-wk MED diet + white button/oyster mushrooms) was null on GAD-7 and POMS tension. One mouse high-fat-diet study of isolated A. bisporus polysaccharides (Fu 2026) reported reduced anxiety-like behavior, but does not overcome three consistent null human A. bisporus RCTs (and oyster mushroom Cha 2026 or Lion's Mane trials test different fungal species). Direction remains open.

No human trial tests roasted Agaricus bisporus on validated apathy scales in Parkinson disease; Glover 2025 (n=41) and Uffelman 2024 (n=60) showed null POMS mood/vigor differences, and Zajac 2020 (n=370) showed null mood outcomes.

Consistent with Round 1 executive function (0691=open), all three direct human Agaricus bisporus RCTs found null effects on attention: Glover 2025 (n=41, 168 g/d cremini) found null RBANS attention (change +4.00 vs +2.29, interaction p=0.705), Uffelman 2024 (n=60, white button+oyster) found null RBANS digit span and coding, and Zajac 2020 (n=370 ITT, white button capsules) found null effects across all cognitive domains. Isolated ergothioneine trials (Zajac 2025 n=147; Yau 2024 n=19 MCI) showed only transient or verbal-learning memory signals without attention gains, and EPIC-Norfolk (Cha 2024) and Singapore DaHA (Feng 2019) pooled unidentified mushroom species cross-sectionally. Direction remains open.

No clinical trial tests cooked Agaricus bisporus on Parkinson bradykinesia. Zhgenti 2026 used an unheated tyrosinase-enriched A. bisporus protein extract to reduce beam-walking errors in MPTP mice (without isolating bradykinesia speed, and cooking denatures tyrosinase per Pretzler 2024), while Tng 2025 tested isolated ergothioneine on 6-OHDA mouse rotations and Drosophila climbing rather than bradykinesia.

In the only human randomized crossover trial testing Agaricus bisporus on bowel function (Hess 2018, PMC6213353, n=32 healthy adults consuming 226 g/d sliced roasted A. bisporus vs 28 g/d meat for 10 days), mushrooms significantly increased fecal wet weight (122.42 vs 94.62 g/stool, p=0.002) and shifted Bacteroidetes/Firmicutes microbiota, but showed NO significant difference in stool frequency (4.25 vs 4.13, p=0.35), Bristol stool consistency (3.12 vs 3.35, p=0.11), or day-1 constipation rating (0.36 vs 0.66, p=0.52), while transiently increasing gas and flatulence on days 1-2 (resolved by day 10). The authors note FDA guidance that greater fecal weight alone does not establish improved bowel function. Mouse DSS-colitis studies (Dempsey 2025, Liu 2024) model colitis rather than constipation. Direction remains open.

No clinical or pharmacokinetic trial evaluates cooked Agaricus bisporus on levodopa daily off time in Parkinson disease; although unheated A. bisporus tyrosinase increased plasma L-DOPA in MPTP mice (Zhgenti 2026), cooking denatures fungal tyrosinase (Pretzler 2024).

No clinical trial evaluates cooked Agaricus bisporus on daytime sleepiness (ESS) in Parkinson disease; Okumura 2025 (n=92) found isolated 8 mg/d ergothioneine had NO significant between-group effect on OSA-MA Factor I Sleepiness on Rising (p=0.276).

All three direct human Agaricus bisporus RCTs (total n=471 analyzed) found completely null effects on depressive symptoms: Zajac 2020 (n=370 ITT, 24-wk white button mushroom capsules) was null on DASS-21 depression, Uffelman 2024 (n=60, 8-wk MED diet + white button/oyster) was null on BDI, PHQ-9, and POMS depression, and Glover 2025 (n=41, 6-wk 168 g/d fresh cremini) was null on BDI-II, PHQ-9, and POMS depression. Observational associations (Ba 2021 NHANES n=24,699 middle-tertile OR 0.31 but highest-tertile null OR 0.91, P-trend=0.42; Park 2022 Korean cohort n=87,822 HR 0.86) pooled unidentified mushroom species (including shiitake/oyster/enoki in Korea) and are outweighed by the null A. bisporus RCTs. Direction remains open.

No clinical or polysomnographic study evaluates roasted Agaricus bisporus on REM sleep behavior disorder or dream enactment frequency; Okumura 2025 (n=92) found isolated 8 mg/d ergothioneine had NO between-group effect on OSA-MA Factor III Frequent Dreaming (p=0.922).

No clinical trial tests cooked Agaricus bisporus on fall frequency in Parkinson disease; UV-exposed A. bisporus vitamin D2 RCTs (Stephensen 2012 n=38; Zajac 2020 n=370; Comboni 2026 n=41) raised 25(OH)D2 while proportionally lowering 25(OH)D3 without preventing winter total 25(OH)D decline or assessing falls.

Direct human Agaricus bisporus RCTs show null effects on fatigue and vitality: Glover 2025 (n=41, 168 g/d fresh cremini) found null POMS fatigue/vigor and SF-36v2 energy/fatigue; Uffelman 2024 (n=60, MED diet + white button/oyster) found no mushroom-specific effect on POMS fatigue or vigor (vigor improved over time in both MED arms); and Shanely 2014 (6-wk UV Portobello A. bisporus D2 powder in athletes) found null muscle function/damage outcomes. Zheng 2025 extended mouse swimming exhaustion using a 3-mushroom polysaccharide blend (Pleurotus eryngii + Agrocybe aegerita + A. bisporus) that does not isolate A. bisporus. Direction remains open.

Three independent double-blind, placebo-controlled human RCTs of oral ergothioneine—a heat-stable fungal antioxidant directly quantified in Agaricus bisporus (Kalaras 2017) and shown to double in human serum after 16 weeks of 100 g/d white button mushroom intake (Calvo 2016, n=37)—oppose the worsening hypothesis and support sleep improvement: Okumura 2025 (Study 2, n=92 OSA-MA analyzed) found 8 mg/d ergothioneine for 16 weeks significantly improved OSA-MA Factor V Sleep Length (+2.7 vs -0.4, p=0.007) and Factor IV Refreshing (+2.5 vs -0.1, p=0.026); Zajac 2025 (n=147 older adults) found 25 mg/d ergothioneine for 16 weeks significantly improved subjective sleep initiation (p<0.05); and Katsube 2022 found 20 mg/d ergothioneine for 4 weeks improved PSQI-J sleep difficulty and objective EEG N2/N1/WASO. Because all trials used isolated ergothioneine at doses higher than typical single culinary A. bisporus servings and enrolled non-PD adults, certainty is capped at minimal_signal.

No clinical trial or autonomic study evaluates roasted Agaricus bisporus on orthostatic hypotension or lightheadedness in Parkinson disease; Uffelman 2024 (PMID:38135005, n=60) reported null seated blood pressure change.

Two human whole-mushroom RCTs failed to show pain improvement from Agaricus bisporus: Glover 2025 (n=41, 6-wk 168 g/d fresh cremini) was null on SF-36v2 bodily pain, and Uffelman 2024 (n=60, 8-wk MED diet + white button/oyster) found greater SF-36v1 pain improvement in the non-mushroom control arm (Time x Group p=0.044, cautioned by baseline pain imbalance 77.6 vs 85.7, p=0.04). Although Ruthes 2013 reported antinociceptive inhibition of formalin-induced licking in mice using purified A. bisporus fucogalactan (ID50 36.0 mg/kg), one isolated-polysaccharide acute mouse assay does not outweigh two null/non-favorable whole-mushroom human RCTs. Direction remains open.

Two independent rodent narrow-beam balance studies specifically using Agaricus bisporus support a minimal preclinical easing signal: Thangthaeng 2015 showed aged Fischer 344 rats fed whole lyophilized A. bisporus (0.5% and 1% diet for 8 weeks; 2% and 5% null) stayed significantly longer on a narrow balance beam, and Zhgenti 2026 showed MPTP Parkinson mice given oral tyrosinase-enriched A. bisporus protein extract for 20 days had significantly fewer beam-walking errors (p<0.001) alongside nigral TH+ preservation and higher plasma L-DOPA/nigral dopamine. Crucial transfer caveats: roasting denatures mushroom tyrosinase (Pretzler 2024), neither study used roasted mushrooms, and no human Parkinson postural-stability trial exists; capped at minimal_signal.

No clinical trial tests cooked Agaricus bisporus on urinary urgency frequency or overactive bladder symptoms. Prostate cancer trials of white button mushroom powder/tablets (Twardowski 2015 Phase I n=36; Wang 2024 suspended Phase II NCT04519879) evaluated serum PSA, circulating MDSCs, and toxicity without reporting urinary urgency or IPSS LUTS endpoints. Historical mouse bladder-implantation carcinogenicity tests of raw mushroom methanol extracts/agaritine (Hashida 1990; reviewed by Lagrange & Vernoux 2020) show heat cooking degrades agaritine and do not measure urinary urgency. Direction remains open.

No clinical or preclinical study evaluates roasted Agaricus bisporus on Parkinson visual hallucination frequency; culinary A. bisporus contains no psilocybin and must not be conflated with hallucinogenic Psilocybe species.

No human gait-speed trial evaluates cooked Agaricus bisporus on walking slowness in Parkinson disease; Zhgenti 2026 assessed beam-walking errors with unheated tyrosinase extract (denatured by cooking) and Shanely 2014 found null muscle function with portobello powder.

Direct full-text inspection of the two coated cantaloupe-SOD (Extramel) human stress RCTs confirms no controlled anxiety reduction: in Milesi 2009 (PMC2757026; n=70 stressed healthy adults, 10 mg/d Extramel x 4 wk), perceived stress (PSS-14) improved vs placebo (p=0.010), but the FARD relational pole and explicit anxiety items ("apprehension", "internal tension", "neurovegetative troubles") were explicitly NULL vs placebo at day 28; in Carillon 2014 (PMC4073155; NCT01767922; n=61, 84 d), PSS-14 improved (D28 p<0.03, D84 p<0.04), whereas the Hamilton Anxiety Scale was used solely as baseline eligibility screening and NOT as an outcome. Preclinical Sayyar 2023 tested ethanol muskmelon SEED extract (wrong plant part) in non-PD rats, Jacquet 2015 (n=87) tested a 4-ingredient burnout blend (TARGET 1), and Dadmehr 2024 is a traditional Persian medicine textbook listing. No raw cantaloupe or PD anxiety trial exists; claim remains open.

No clinical trial has evaluated raw cantaloupe or melon-SOD extracts on clinical apathy severity in Parkinson disease. In the closest human motivation proxy—Houghton 2011 (n=38 women aged 50-65 y, 12-wk DB RCT of 500 mg/d gliadin-combined melon SOD vs placebo)—Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory (MFI) "reduced motivation" and "reduced activity" subscales were explicitly NULL (all p>0.05). Neither Milesi 2009 (n=70 Extramel), Carillon 2014 (n=61 Extramel), nor Koike 2022 (PMC9143343 orthopedic GliSODin RCT) measured apathy. Claim remains open.
